modes.label: CPU Cloud (published floor)
modes.note: Exact CPU/RAM/storage bundle and host/region must be selected live; do not treat the floor as a universal SKU.

modes.label: Instant VMs
modes.note: Pre-configured beta; no separate public tariff was exposed on the audited homepage/dashboard.

caveats: Full root OS control, dedicated passthrough GPU, Linux/Windows and Docker templates. GPU price is set per host (the published "From" price is the floor); CPU $0.003/vCPU-h, RAM $0.002/GB-h, storage $0.00005/GB-h ($0.0365/GB-month, also billed while stopped) and dedicated IPv4 $0.006/h ($4.38/month) are flat calculator constants on the deploy page. $5 deposit; zero balance automatically deletes servers.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null (A100 with unverified VRAM, spot) stay unpriced, not free. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. On-demand GPU VMs are ordinary GPU instances (no alt flag); marketplace availability is shown via the stock flag.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.
GPU rates are marketplace floors ("From $X/hr"): a specific host/region can cost more, and the cheapest host may be sold out. Estimates are a lower bound.

fleet.verification: Prepaid balance; official homepage says start with $5.
fleet.notes: Provider advertises no quotas or commitments. No finite fresh-account GPU/VM maximum asserted; marketplace stock and credit balance still constrain a fleet. Independent verification/review requirements not published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

harness_api.note: Plain KVM GPU VM marketplace; API v2 only manages VM lifecycle. No agent harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: Deployment Options: Use location-based deployment for automatic hostnode selection and simplified setup, or choose direct hostnode deployment for full control over placement, port configuration, and resource allocation.
ingress_rules.note: Only port selection: hostnode-based deploys can use NAT port forwarding ('port_forwards': [{internal_port, external_port}]), so only mapped ports are reachable. Dedicated-IP / Core Compute VMs expose everything: 'By default, all ports on your Linux VMs are open, and UFW is disabled.' (https://docs.tensordock.com/virtual-machines/opening-ports-on-core-compute-vms). No provider IP allowlist, private URLs or security groups.

guest_firewall.quote: The following steps are for securing your VM with the UFW firewall, to help protect your VM.
guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VM with root; docs recommend in-guest UFW (Linux) / Windows Defender Firewall as the way to restrict ports.

secret_proxy.quote: SSH keys are used for instance authentication, while SECRET types store sensitive values that are never returned via the API.
secret_proxy.note: Org secret store (SSH keys + generic secrets, write-only via API); SSH keys are auto-added to Linux deployments. No credential-injecting egress proxy documented.

isolation.quote: KVM Isolation - Every virtual machine is fully isolated from all other VMs on the hostnode to prevent interference.

image_oci.note: VM instances (the product modeled by this card) boot from fixed OS templates (Ubuntu/Windows), not a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image. TensorDock's separate 'Managed GPU Containers' product does accept a Docker image from a public/private registry, but that is a different, unpriced product not represented in this card's modes.

desktop.quote: This tutorial helps users on the TensorDock Marketplace connect to an instance on Windows through a Remote Desktop Protocol.
desktop.note: Windows VMs are reachable via RDP; docs also cover installing Parsec/Moonlight/Sunshine for GPU desktop streaming.

browser.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — TensorDock ships bare GPU/CPU VMs, not a managed/provided browser.

computer_use.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click driving API is documented.

anti_bot.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — TensorDock is a GPU/CPU VM marketplace, not a browser-automation/stealth product.

captcha_solving.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — plain GPU/CPU VM marketplace, no CAPTCHA-solving service.

egress_ip_type.quote: All TensorDock Core Compute VMs enjoy per-VM dedicated IPs.
egress_ip_type.note: Dedicated/static IPv4 per VM ($0.006/h) from datacenter-hosted GPU hosts; not residential/mobile.

snapshot.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
snapshot.note: Instance Management API exposes only start/stop/delete/modify; no snapshot or checkpoint endpoint is documented for VMs.

snapshot_auto.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
snapshot_auto.note: No automatic state snapshot on stop/timeout is documented; disk simply persists (billed while stopped).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API endpoint exists in the documented Instance Management or Instance Creation endpoints.

fork.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
fork.note: No clone/fork endpoint documented in the API.

fork_running.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
fork_running.note: not offered: no fork capability exists at all, so cloning a running machine is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance / Modify Instance
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no fork/snapshot capability of any kind is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Stop Instance - Stop a running instance / Start Instance - Start a stopped instance
pause_resume.note: Stopping a VM halts compute billing while storage continues to be billed (disk_billed_when_stopped); Start resumes it. No memory-preserving suspend is claimed.

wake_on_request.quote: Start Instance - Start a stopped instance
wake_on_request.note: Starting a stopped instance requires an explicit API/dashboard action; no automatic wake-on-incoming-request behavior is documented.

volume_attach.quote: All Core Compute locations include several features, including network storage.
volume_attach.note: Storage is a single per-VM disk sized at creation/modify time (storage_gb); no separate attachable extra-volume API is documented.

volume_shared.quote: a VM deployed in our Manassas, Virginia location once stopped, will be available to deploy on any Manassas, Virginia servers that have that GPU available
volume_shared.note: Network storage lets a stopped VM's own disk redeploy to another hostnode in the same location; it is not a volume mounted by several running machines simultaneously.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Stop Instance - Stop a running instance
auto_stop_idle.note: Stopping is a manual/API action; no idle-detection auto-stop is documented (only a zero prepaid balance auto-deletes servers).

live_resize.quote: Modify Instance - Modify the resources of a stopped or stopped-disassociated instance. Instance must be in 'Stopped' or 'StoppedDisassociated' state
live_resize.note: Resizing vCPU/RAM/GPU requires the instance to be stopped first; not a live/running resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: Running Jupyter Notebook / Running Stable Diffusion in Docker / Running SimpleTuner/Flux
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: templates cover ML tooling (Jupyter, Stable Diffusion), not coding-agent harnesses like Claude Code/Codex.

own_agent_api.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — TensorDock provides raw compute, not its own browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.quote: Our RESTful API allows you to programmatically manage virtual machines, monitor resources, and integrate with your existing infrastructure.
mcp_server.note: Only a REST API (v2) is documented; no MCP server is offered.

lang_python.quote: Select any TensorML installation ... Type the following command in your TensorDock instance to run Jupyter Notebook: $ jupyter notebook --ip=0.0.0.0
lang_python.note: TensorML preconfigured images ship Python/Jupyter/CUDA stacks out of the box.

inbound_https.quote: All TensorDock Core Compute VMs enjoy per-VM dedicated IPs. This allows your machine to enjoy a full range of ports... By default, all ports on your Linux VMs are open, and UFW is disabled.
inbound_https.note: Access is via raw dedicated IP + arbitrary ports/your own TLS; there is no provider-managed HTTPS URL/ingress feature.

egress_allowlist.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — full root VM with no provider-side outbound allow/deny list documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented.

macos.quote: Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux with SSH access) / Windows 10 (Windows with RDP access)
macos.note: not offered: only Linux and Windows OS templates are documented; no macOS VMs.

arm64.quote: The latest Intel Xeon and AMD EPYC processors for scientific computing and HPC workloads.
arm64.note: not offered: CPU/GPU fleet is described as Intel Xeon/AMD EPYC (x86-64) hosts; no ARM instance type is advertised.

self_host.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — TensorDock is a hosted marketplace service, not software you self-host.

byoc.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — VMs run on TensorDock's/partner hosts' infrastructure, not deployed into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: The industry's most cost-effective virtual machine infrastructure for deep learning, AI and rendering.
open_source.note: not offered: no OSI-licensed core product is published; TensorDock's platform is proprietary.

soc2.quote: TensorDock aggregates GPUs from Tier 3/4 data centers with certifications ranging from SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.
soc2.note: The SOC 2/PCI/ISO27001/HIPAA mentions describe partner datacenters' certifications, not a SOC 2 attestation of TensorDock itself; no TensorDock-issued SOC 2 report is offered.

hipaa.quote: TensorDock aggregates GPUs from Tier 3/4 data centers with certifications ranging from SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.
hipaa.note: HIPAA is referenced as a datacenter partner certification, not a BAA offered by TensorDock; no TensorDock BAA/HIPAA-eligibility program is documented.

sso.quote: Fine-grained Access Control - Our IAM system allows you to manage who from your organization can access what and when, through our dashboard and API.
sso.note: Access control is via TensorDock's own IAM/dashboard, not SAML/OIDC single sign-on; no SSO integration is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Hundreds of GPUs ready to deploy on our dashboard at any time, distributed across 100+ locations in over 20 countries.
eu_data_residency.note: Marketplace hosts span 100+ locations/20+ countries including Europe, so an EU-region host/location can be selected at deploy time; no dedicated EU-only guarantee page found.

max_session_h.quote: Start Instance / Stop Instance / Delete Instance
max_session_h.note: No maximum runtime is documented; VMs run until stopped/deleted or the prepaid balance reaches zero (which auto-deletes servers).
